source_snapshot.items_direct_xlsx: Boot Time Post Package Repair with Uncorrectable Errors
source_snapshot.procedure_direct_xlsx: 【Before Test】 1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition. 2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.). 3. The following BIOS settings paths are from the Intel reference platform. Locations of these settings may be different on your BIOS implementation Customer Scripts (CScripts) Enabling The following is a quick reference of the key BIOS knobs for CScripts: • EDKII > Socket Configuration > Processor Configuration > Lock Chipset = Disable • EDKII > Socket Configuration > Processor Configuration > MSR Lock Control = Disable • EDKII > Socket Configuration > IIO Configuration > DFX Global Configuration > — EV DFX Features = Enable — Disable BIOS Done = [X] ELOG Enabling • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > eMCA Settings > — EMCA Error Support= Enable — EMCA Logging Support= Enable — Corrected Error eLog = Enable — Memory Error eLog = Enable — Processor Error eLog = Enable Error Reporting Enabling • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > WHEA Settings > — WHEA Support = Enable — WHEA Log Memory Error = Enable — WHEA Log Processor Error = Enable — WHEA Log PCI Error = Enable Error Injection Enabling • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > — System Errors = Enable — System Memory Poison = Enable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Error Injection Settings > — MCA Bank Error Injection Support = Enable — WHEA Error Injection Support = Enable — WHEA PCIe* Error Injection Support = Enable — WHEA PCIe* Error Action Table = Enable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > IIO Error Enabling > — IIO/PCH Global Error Support = Enable — IIO MCA Support = Disable — IIO eDPC Support = Disable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > PCIE Error Enabling > PCIe* Corrected Error Threshold Counter = Disable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > PCIE Error Enabling > PCIe AER Corrected Errors = Enable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > EMCA Settings > LMCE Support = Enable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Memory Error Enabling > Memory Corrected Error = Enable • EDKII > Socket Configuration > Uncore Configuration > Uncore General Configuration > Directory Mode Enable = Disable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > Miscellaneous Configuration > Enable DAM Pin = Enable Firmware First Model • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > EMCA Settings > — EMCA Logging Support = Enable — EMCA CMCI-SMI Morphing = EMCA gen2 CSMI — EMCA CMCI-SMI Threshold = 0 — EMCA MCA-SMI Enable = EMCA gen 2 - MSMI • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > IIO Error Enabling > OS Native AER Support = Disable Crash Log • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Crash Log Enabling > CPU CrashLog Feature = Disable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Crash Log Enabling > PCH CrashLog Feature = Disable 4. Other OS Notes You can use grub2-mkconfig to specify "ras=cec_disable" by modifying /etc/default/grub's "GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX" with "ras=cec_disable". 【During Test】 1. PPR Uncorrectable Errors specific BIOS setup : • EDKII > Socket Configuration > Memory Configuration > — DDR PPR Type = Soft PPR — Force PPR On All DRAM For UCE = Enabled — Attempt Fast Boot = Enable — Attempt Fast Cold Boot = Enable • If fast boot knobs are not enabled then BIOS will skip loading NVRAM and there'll be no PPR entries for boot time PPR. • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > — RAS Log Level = MID (BASIC_FLOW, FUNC_FLOW) • EDKII > Platform Configuration > Miscellaneous Configuration > — Serial Debug Message Level = Normal 1. Halt the system and reset the injectors. >>> halt() >>> ei.utils.resetInjectorLockCheck() 2. Inject an uncorrectable error then resume the system so the BIOS can log the DIMM error record. The system should reset on its own due to UC error. >>> ei.mem.injectMemError(0x0, errType="uce") >>> go() 3. Observe in serial log that BIOS qualified the bad row for PPR. 4. The system should now have rebooted, then observe that a DDR PPR request is present in the serial log; fast boot is disabled now. 5. Observe in serial log that PPR took action on the UC error and that the PprRepairStatus passed.

test_case.test_name: Boot Time Post Package Repair with Uncorrectable Errors — retained controlled review-layer procedure
test_case.purpose: Demonstrate that an injected uncorrectable memory error on the intended GNR DRAM row triggers the expected reset and boot-time Soft PPR flow, with firmware qualifying and repairing the row and reporting passed PprRepairStatus.
required_package: GNR stepping, BIOS/BMC/OS and exact DIMM/DRAM-row topology
CScripts harness version/hash/license and address0x0 UCE target semantics
Project mapping/restoration for all source BIOS/GRUB/DFX/ELog/WHEA/PPR/fast-boot/serial knobs
Expected UCE MCA/reset signature and maximum reset/POST/boot time
Serial fields identifying bad row, DDR PPR request, fast-boot disable, action and PprRepairStatus
Dedicated window, data/workload isolation and independent OOB/BIOS recovery
test_case.test_command: Record platform/DIMM topology, harness and settings baseline; apply/verify the complete source enablement plus Soft PPR, Force-PPR-UCE, fast-boot and serial knobs; prove what harness address0x0 targets; preserve logs and establish continuous serial/OOB capture; halt/reset injector, issue one exact UCE and `go()`; attribute the automatic reset to that UCE, retain serial across boot, identify the same bad row, DDR PPR request, fast-boot state, repair action and passed status; verify DIMM/OS/BMC health and restore temporary settings without reinjection.
test_case.expected_result: Serial log that PPR took action on the UC error and that the PprRepairStatus passed.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: No executable PASS verdict exists yet for Boot Time Post Package Repair with Uncorrectable Errors. The protected Criteria is `Serial log that PPR took action on the UC error and that the PprRepairStatus passed.`; it becomes enforceable only after resolving: Resolve Reliability row161 Wistron-System RAS-00118-V002: approve GNR/BIOS/BMC/OS, CScripts version/hash/license, address0x0-to-socket/IMC/channel/DIMM/DRAM-row mapping and expected UCE MCA/reset signature; map/restore every source BIOS/GRUB/DFX/Soft-PPR/Force-PPR/fast-boot/serial knob; define reset/POST/boot timeouts, continuous serial bad-row/DDR-PPR/fast-boot/action/PprRepairStatus fields, same-row correlation and OOB recovery with no automatic reset or reinjection.
safety_gate: Use only a dedicated workload-free SUT and approved sacrificial row
Do not inject at 0x0 until the vendor harness proves its physical target and non-OS semantics
Preserve all logs/settings and arm serial/OOB capture before halt/injection
Issue exactly one UCE; stop on wrong target/severity, missing reset, reset loop, POST failure or failed/absent PPR status
Do not reset or reinject automatically when the expected reset fails
Restore all debug/security/PPR settings only after evidence capture and verify final DIMM/OS/BMC health
expected_evidence: Platform/DIMM/row identity, harness and before/after settings matrix
Address0x0 target proof and one exact UCE injector transcript
Expected UCE MCA/reset cause plus reset/POST/boot timeline
Continuous serial bad-row qualification and DDR PPR request with fast-boot state
Same-row PPR action and passed PprRepairStatus
Supporting ELog/OS/SEL, final health/restoration and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: Fast-boot transitions and Force-PPR scope are firmware-specific and require explicit expected before/after state; no CE or row160 procedure may substitute for this UCE path.
